instructions.name: callback_deal
docs: The oracle's answer: shuffle the line and seat the first six.

accounts.name: vrf_program_identity
docs: Scoped VRF identity PDA, bound to this program. Its presence as a signer proves
the callback was issued by the VRF program for this program.

instructions.name: callback_round
docs: The oracle's answer: draw the rule, group the answers, cull.

accounts.name: vrf_program_identity
docs: Scoped VRF identity PDA, bound to this program. Its presence as a signer proves
the callback was issued by the VRF program for this program.

instructions.name: close_round
docs: Close the round and ask the oracle which way it is scored.
Permissionless once the clock runs out, so a room cannot be held open by
a player who benefits from waiting.

accounts.name: payer
docs: Anyone may close a round once the clock has run out. Leaving it to the
players would let whoever benefits from waiting simply not act.

instructions.name: create_room
docs: Open a room. Base layer.

accounts.name: vault
docs: Holds the stakes, and is never delegated to a rollup.

accounts.name: answers
docs: The sealed half. Delegated with the room, then made unreadable.

instructions.name: deal
docs: Ask the oracle to fill a room from the line.

instructions.name: delegate_room
docs: Hand the room and its answers to a rollup. Base layer.
`validator` pins which one. Passing the TEE identity is what makes the
answers secret; on a plain rollup the room is fast but readable, which
defeats the entire point of moving it.

accounts.name: authority
docs: The host, or the host's session key. Pays the delegation rent, which is
why it must be writable.

accounts.name: room
docs: verified inside `delegate_account`.

accounts.name: answers
docs: whose answers are still on Solana would be readable by anyone.

instructions.name: enter_queue
docs: Pay a stake and wait to be put somewhere you did not choose.

instructions.name: finish_room
docs: Push the finished room back to Solana so the pot can be paid.

instructions.name: join_room
docs: Take a seat and pay the stake. Base layer.
`session` is a throwaway key the app holds. It signs answers inside the
rollup so a fifteen-second round does not need a fingerprint, and it can
do nothing else.
`ending_vote` is this player's say in what happens if the room comes
down to two: share the pot, or let the oracle pick one. Majority at the
door decides it for the whole table, ties go to a split.

instructions.name: leave_queue
docs: Stop waiting, and take the stake back.

instructions.name: leave_room
docs: Take your seat back and your stake with it. Base layer, open rooms only.

instructions.name: lock_room
docs: Close the door and start round one. Base layer, host only.

accounts.name: authority
docs: The host, or the host's session key. Checked in the handler because
either is acceptable and `has_one` can only express one of them.

instructions.name: open_public_room
docs: Build a public table. Once, ever - dealt rooms are reused.

instructions.name: open_queue
docs: Open the line for a given stake. Once per price.

accounts.name: vault
docs: Holds everybody's stake until they are dealt somewhere.

instructions.name: seal_room
docs: Seal the room so nobody can read the answers. Runs inside the rollup.

instructions.name: settle
docs: Pay the survivors. Base layer.

accounts.name: caller
docs: Anyone may trigger the payout. It pays the survivors and nobody else,
whoever asks, so there is no reason to gate it - and gating it would let
a sore loser refuse to pay by doing nothing.

instructions.name: submit_answer
docs: Lock in an answer. Runs inside the rollup, signed by the session key.

accounts.name: session
docs: The throwaway key registered at join. It signs answers and nothing else -
it cannot join, cannot settle, cannot touch the vault.

types.name: Answers
docs: What everyone said this round. Sealed, and delegated alongside the room.
Split from `Room` for one reason: a sealed account is invisible over RPC to
everybody, which is exactly right for answers and useless for everything
else. Players still need to see the round number, the clock and who is left,
so the public half of the game stays in `Room` and only the words move here.
The program running inside the rollup reads this normally - sealing gates
RPC, not execution, which was worth confirming before relying on it.

fields.name: round
docs: The round these words belong to. Cleared between rounds so a stale
answer cannot be counted twice.

types.name: Ending
docs: Which way this round is scored.
Drawn by VRF *after* every answer is sealed, which is the entire defence
against collusion: a bloc that agrees on one answer is the largest group,
and half the time being the largest group is what kills you.
How a room settles when it comes down to two.
Two players carry no signal. "Match the herd" needs a herd, and with two
people left same-word and different-word are symmetric under both rules - no
rule can separate them, so every heads-up round culls nobody. Something has
to break the symmetry, and rather than picking one for everybody, the table
picks its own before a word is played.

types.name: Outcome
docs: How a round ended.
The rule itself never changes: the smallest group strayed from the herd and
goes. This records whether that actually happened, because it cannot always
- if every group is the same size then nobody is odd, and a round where
nobody is odd has to say so rather than looking like a round that failed.

types.name: Queue
docs: The line for public rooms.
You pay to stand in it and the oracle decides where you end up. That is the
whole point: a room you cannot choose is a room you cannot fill with your
friends, which is what makes the simple rule safe to keep. Everything else
about a dealt room plays exactly like a private one.

fields.name: stake
docs: What a seat costs here. One queue per price.

fields.name: awaiting_deal
docs: A deal has been asked of the oracle and not yet delivered. Blocks a
second one: two live deals over the same line would seat some people
twice and others never.

fields.name: dealing_into
docs: Which public room the outstanding deal is for.

fields.name: host_session
docs: The host's session key, allowed to run the room but never to spend it.
Locking the door and handing the room to a rollup are not money
decisions - they cannot move a lamport, and the host has already
committed by paying to open the room. Making them need the wallet meant
two more fingerprints in the middle of setting up a game, for no security
anyone was getting. The session key does them instead. It still cannot
take a seat, settle, or touch the vault.

fields.name: stake
docs: Per player, paid once at the door. The pot never grows after that.

fields.name: round_ends_at
docs: Unix time after which the round can be closed by anyone.

fields.name: outcome
docs: How the round that just finished ended.

fields.name: ending
docs: The table's answer to "what happens at two", tallied when the door
closes and fixed from then on - so nobody picks the ending once they can
see who they would be picking it against.

fields.name: dealt
docs: Seated by the oracle out of the public queue, rather than opened by a
person who shared a code.
A dealt room has no host to run it - the seats were assigned, nobody
invited anybody - so the jobs a host normally does are open to any player
sitting in it. None of them can move money.

fields.name: coin_decided
docs: Whether the last two were separated by the coin rather than by the herd.
Worth a byte. Without it a player who reached the final two and lost
cannot tell whether the room out-guessed them or a coin did, and "you
are out" with no reason reads as a bug rather than as a game.

fields.name: awaiting_coin
docs: A coin flip has been asked of the oracle and not yet delivered.
The only randomness left in a game. Rounds are decided by the room, so
they need nothing from an oracle; the flip between the final two does,
and only when the table voted for one.

fields.name: last_round
docs: What everyone said in the round that just finished, and which round that
was.
Published deliberately. Answers are secret while the window is open,
because seeing them would let you copy the crowd and there would be no
game - but the moment a round is scored that reason is gone, and seeing
who said what is the best part of it. So the resolved round's words are
copied out of the sealed account into this one, where anybody can read
them.

fields.name: wallet
docs: Pays the stake and receives the payout.

fields.name: session
docs: Signs answers inside the rollup so a 15-second round does not need a
fingerprint. It can do nothing else - see `submit_answer`.

fields.name: answered_round
docs: The round this seat last answered in.
Public on purpose. Seeing that someone has answered is most of the
tension in a fifteen-second round; seeing *what* they answered would end
the game. The text lives in `Answers`, which nobody can read.

fields.name: has_answered
docs: Whether `answered_round` refers to a real answer rather than seat zero
never having played.

fields.name: ending_vote
docs: What this player wants to happen if they reach the final two. Cast at
the door, before they know who they would be facing.

types.name: Vault
docs: Holds the stakes. Never delegated to a rollup.
That is not a detail, it is the security argument. The room goes to a rollup
so answers can be sealed and rounds can be fast; the money stays on Solana.
A rollup that misbehaves can decide the game wrongly, and still cannot move a
lamport - payouts happen here, from state the rollup has committed back and
this program has checked.

types.name: Waiting
docs: Somebody waiting to be dealt into a room.
